key_facts: A **small painful crusted nodule on the helix or antihelix**, worse lying on that side, in an older adult.
**Pressure on cartilage** with poor blood supply → inflammation and cartilage damage (‘a pressure sore of the ear’).
**Pressure-relief pillow / ear protector for 4–6 weeks**; consider potent topical steroid; refer if failing or atypical.
**SCC or BCC of the ear**; **keratoacanthoma** (rapid crater); **tophaceous gout**.

sections.title: Overview
blocks: A benign, **painful**, inflamed nodule of the ear cartilage and overlying skin. It is commonest on the **helix in older men** and on the **antihelix in women**.

The pinna is a **high-risk site for skin cancer**: it is sun-exposed and thin-skinned, and spread to the parotid and cervical nodes happens early. BAD 2020 classifies **ear cSCC as high-risk by site**.

sections.title: Aetiology: causes and risk factors
blocks: **Pressure-induced ischaemia.** Ear cartilage has little subcutaneous padding and a poor blood supply. Sustained pressure (sleeping on one side, headsets, phones, hats), cold or sun damage causes perichondrial inflammation and focal cartilage necrosis that extrudes through the skin. **One-sided sleeping is typical, e.g. after a stroke, or with arthritis or CPAP masks.** In [Case 2](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) with a previous right-sided stroke, ask which side she lies on.
Chronic UV (helix, especially in men with short hair), immunosuppression, and for gout, urate deposition in cool tissue.

fig.caption: Chondrodermatitis: a tender crusted nodule on the upper ear rim. First line is offloading with a foam ear protector or pillow with a hole, for at least 4–6 weeks.
fig.alt: Ear with a crusted rim nodule beside a foam ring pillow

ul: A firm, round, 4–10 mm nodule with a **central crust, scale or keratin plug**, sometimes ulcerated.
**Exquisitely tender**: it wakes the patient at night when they lie on it, and **light squeezing causes disproportionate pain** (the course bedside test). Usually on the side the patient sleeps on.

sections.title: Diagnosis and investigations

ul: Clinical: site + pain + central crust + sleeping history.
Dermoscopy: central white-yellow keratin/ulcer with a radiating whitish "starburst" and peripheral dotted or linear vessels. It is **non-specific** and **cannot reliably exclude SCC/BCC**.

**Biopsy when:** atypical features (rapid growth, bleeding, induration, a size >1 cm, a rolled pearly edge, no pain); no improvement after **6–8 weeks of strict offloading**; immunosuppression; or patient anxiety.

blocks: Pain pattern, growth tempo, and palpation of regional nodes. Biopsy anything unexplained. Serum urate (when not in an acute flare) if tophi are suspected.

sections.title: Differential diagnoses

ddx.name: cSCC
ddx.f: Indurated, keratotic / ulcerated, growing; often painless ± node.

ddx.name: Chilblain / relapsing polychondritis
ddx.f: Cold, bilateral / whole ear red sparing lobe.

blocks: See *Ear nodule differentials* (SCC, BCC, keratoacanthoma, AK, gouty tophi, also cutaneous horn, wart, elastotic nodules of the ear, weathering nodules, chilblain).
As above. Also chilblain (cold, bilateral, purple), relapsing polychondritis (the whole ear red, sparing the lobe), and discoid lupus.

sections.title: Management
blocks: **Step 1: pressure relief, for everyone (first-line; the course answer)**

ul: A **pressure-relieving device**: a CNH prosthesis/"ear protector" made of foam with a hole for the ear (sold OTC and online), a pillow with a hole, or a travel pillow; sleep on the other side. Remove headphone and phone pressure.
Resolution or major improvement occurs in a large proportion of patients within weeks to months. Recurrence is common if offloading stops.
Analgesia as needed. Emollient/protective dressing over the crust.

head: Option
Notes
rows: Low-quality evidence. IP-prescribable (e.g. betamethasone valerate 0.1%) for a short trial **only once SCC/BCC has been reasonably excluded**

Off-label. Small studies show benefit via vasodilatation. Headache and hypotension. **Check PDE-5 inhibitor co-prescription** (contraindicated). Not routinely available as a dermatology product in the UK
Surgical excision of the abnormal cartilage ± skin

blocks: **Refer:** **NG12 1.7.4** says to consider a suspected cancer pathway referral if SCC is suspected (a growing, indurated, bleeding, non-tender or atypical ear nodule). Refer routinely if CNH is not settling after 6–8 weeks of offloading.

ul: **Suspected SCC or keratoacanthoma:** NG12 1.7.4, consider a **suspected cancer pathway referral**. BAD guidance is to **treat KA as SCC** (excise) because they cannot be reliably distinguished clinically.
Suspected BCC: NG12 1.7.5, routine referral, unless the site or size makes delay important (1.7.6). The ear is a high-risk "H-zone" site.
Gouty tophi: a GP/IP gout pathway. **Urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol, treat to target <360 µmol/L, or <300 if tophaceous)**, per NICE NG219 (gout, 2022). Review diuretics.
AK: cross-reference the [older skin pages](condition:itch-xerosis-older-adults) notes see *Worked cases* (field therapy).

ladder.t: **Foam ear protector** (OTC / online), pillow with a hole or travel pillow; sleep on the other side; remove headset / phone pressure. At least a month; recurrence common if offloading stops.
Potent topical steroid; intralesional triamcinolone (trained; atrophy risk) via GP / GPwSI / dermatology.
Failing or atypical: biopsy / surgery (cartilage excision).

blocks.title: Prescribing limits and pitfalls
list: **Aspirin**: Don’t stop for minor skin surgery (BSDS 2023).

refer.t: Rapidly growing, ulcerating or bleeding ear nodule, or with a nearby node: **suspected SCC** (NG12).
No improvement after 6–8 weeks of strict offloading: biopsy.

sections.title: Red flags and when to refer

ul: Rapidly growing, ulcerating or bleeding ear nodule, or an ear nodule with a nearby lymph node: **suspected SCC**, suspected-cancer referral (NICE NG12).

pearls: [Case 2](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) medicines: aspirin is relevant only if a biopsy or excision is done. **Do not stop aspirin for minor skin surgery** (BSDS 2023; see the [skin surgery](condition:skin-surgery-preop) notes). Losartan and simvastatin are not causative.
Explain the mechanism ("a pressure sore of the ear cartilage"). Adherence to offloading for at least a month is the key to success.
**Painless** ear nodule plus rapid growth means think SCC/KA. **Very painful at night** means think CNH. But both can coexist, which is why non-resolving CNH gets a biopsy.
Check transplant or immunosuppressant history (azathioprine, ciclosporin, tacrolimus): cSCC risk rises up to 65–100× in organ transplant recipients.

quiz.a: Painful ear nodule waking them when lying on that side.
Pressure relief (ear protector / pillow with a hole) for 4–6+ weeks.
Atypical features or no improvement after 6–8 weeks.

quiz.q: Painless rapidly growing crater on the ear?
